title: Logo relationships

location.series: IBM Logo Guidelines for Strategic Partners / Version 1.2 / copyright 2023

slide_intent: Clarify who is communicating and providing the offer so audiences do not mistake a partner message for an IBM message.
strategic_value: A visibly subordinate IBM role can support partnership recognition without obscuring the partner’s ownership.
demonstration: The text-only page states source-of-communication principles, CTA ownership and the requirement to explain IBM’s role.
practical_value: Set the partner brand as the communication owner, including the destination of calls to action.

content_islands.name: Clarity and context
content_islands.spec: Place the main explanation under its bold subheading, followed by the two explicit clarity requirements and the conceptual-example note.

reference_purposes.Intent: The source explains that the audience needs to know who it is doing business with and avoid confusion over the source of goods.
reference_purposes.Application: Use the partner’s visual system and direct CTAs to the partner’s website or telephone number.
reference_purposes.Constraint: IBM must occupy a subordinate position, and the scope of its contribution and the source of the communication must both be clear.

ingredient.name: Partner-led brand hierarchy
ingredient.role: Identify the communication owner while acknowledging IBM’s contribution.
ingredient.application: Lead with the partner identity and route CTAs to the partner; position IBM subordinately and explain its role.
ingredient.scope: Marketing materials produced by strategic partners under this guide, not an instruction for IBM-owned communications.
